deep.reconstruction:
This slip is a small record of experimental data, not a derivation. It is headed 'Phys. 4' (an archival or physics-group label). It records two numbered trials from what the bundle title ('PH.Induktion') indicates are electromagnetic-induction experiments, presumably the Gauss–Weber work at Göttingen in the 1830s with magnetometers or induction coils.

Row 1: 'No 27. Entfernung von der Mitte 2100 | doppelter Ausschlag 655.51'. Trial no. 27 was made at a distance from the centre (Mitte) of d = 2100. The units are not stated; they are probably millimetres or scale units. The observed 'double deflection' (doppelter Ausschlag) was A27 = 655.51 scale divisions. A double deflection is the full arc between the two turning points, or equivalently the difference of readings taken with the inducing action reversed. Taking it doubles the effect and cancels the zero-point error.

Row 2: '88 . . . . . | . 863.68'. The ditto dots mean trial no. 88 was made under the same entry, i.e. at the same distance 2100. It gave a double deflection A88 = 863.68.

No computation is written on the page. My own implicit comparisons are:
- ratio A88/A27 = 863.68/655.51 ≈ 1.3176
- difference A88 − A27 = 208.17
- the single (half) deflections would be 327.755 and 431.84.

Why the two values differ at the same distance cannot be determined from this slip alone. Possible reasons include a different coil, number of turns, inductor, or circuit resistance, or a different date. The circled '(29)' is the folio number. The pencil note at lower left ('30b/29' or similar, struck through) is an archival or ordering mark.
